exercise.name: Barbell Power Snatch
aliases: Barbell snatch from the floor, power

reference.title: Barbell Power Snatch
reference.listing: Video (title from the listing URL; the page could not be read from this environment, gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy, so the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)

exercise.bodyPart: Full body (hips, thighs, upper back, shoulders)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace at the floor, hold through the pull and catch; breathe out once the bar is fixed overhead.
breathing.cadence: First pull about 0.8 s, jump and catch about 0.55 s

prescription.frequency: 1-3 times a week, early in the session
prescription.tempo: Controlled first pull, explosive second pull, fast punch under
prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen: technique-limited, every rep fast (NSCA guidance for power exercises).
prescription.progression: Add load in small steps once the overhead catch is stable.

cues.text: Wide snatch grip (bar in the hip crease when standing), feet hip width, hips a little lower than in a deadlift, chest up, back flat.
Push the floor away; the bar slides up the shins and the thighs with the back angle held.
Jump and shrug as the bar reaches the hips, pull the elbows high and out, then punch under and lock the arms overhead in a quarter squat.
Stand up with the bar over the back of the neck, arms locked.
Lower the bar to the hips under control, then to the floor like a deadlift.

mistakes.mistake: Bar swinging away from the body
mistakes.fix: Keep the bar close; brush the hips.

mistakes.mistake: Pressing the bar out at the catch
mistakes.fix: Punch under fast and lock the elbows as the feet land.

mistakes.mistake: Catching with the bar in front of the head
mistakes.fix: Finish with the bar over the back of the neck, over the mid-foot.
Arms long until the hips have finished the jump.

kinematics.norm: Floor start with a wide grip; first pull with the back angle held (clinical opinion; NSCA power clean guide for the pull)
Power catch overhead in a quarter squat on locked arms (clinical opinion)
Wide snatch grip, bar in the hip crease when standing (clinical opinion)
Controlled first pull, explosive second pull (clinical opinion)

cautions: Learn the snatch with a dowel or empty bar under coaching; use bumper plates and a clear platform.
Know how to miss: push the bar away and step out from under it.
Shoulder pain overhead or poor overhead mobility: use high pulls instead.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Hang power snatch for a shorter pull.
Grip: hook grip or straps for the pull.
